stem: A child is suspected to have aspirated a foreign body. Which radiological finding is most suggestive of an obstructing bronchial foreign body?

options.text: Hyperinflation of one lung with flattening of the diaphragm and mediastinal shift

explanation: An obstructing bronchial foreign body can act as a ball-valve obstruction, leading to air trapping. On chest radiograph this may appear as unilateral hyperinflation, flattening of the diaphragm, and mediastinal shift away from the affected side.

optionExplanations.A: This is not a typical feature of foreign body aspiration.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Air trapping from bronchial obstruction causes unilateral hyperinflation, diaphragm flattening, and possible mediastinal shift.
optionExplanations.C: Pleural effusion is not the classic radiographic pattern of airway foreign body aspiration.
optionExplanations.D: These findings suggest cardiac failure rather than foreign body aspiration.
optionExplanations.E: Cavitation suggests infection or necrotising pneumonia, not the usual initial radiographic sign of aspiration.

combinedRecord.question_text_html: Which of the following is true for foreign body radiological imaging?

options.label: A
options.text: PA and Lateral Plain films can help distinguish between airway and oesophageal foreign bodies
options.text_html: PA and Lateral Plain films can help distinguish between airway and oesophageal foreign bodies

options.label: B
options.text: Up to 50% of foreign bodies are radio-opaque
options.text_html: Up to 50% of foreign bodies are radio-opaque

options.label: C
options.text: Subtle radiological changes can include hyperinflation with flattening of the diaphragm or mediastinal shift
options.text_html: Subtle radiological changes can include hyperinflation with flattening of the diaphragm or mediastinal shift

options.label: D
options.text: If a circular object on plain film has a “double ring” or “halo” sign, it is a button battery until proven otherwise and must be treated as an emergency
options.text_html: If a circular object on plain film has a “double ring” or “halo” sign, it is a button battery until proven otherwise and must be treated as an emergency

options.label: E
options.text: Foreign body obstruction of a bronchus/bronchi can cause localised atelectasis and pneumonia
